abstract: Vps13 is a member of the bridge-like lipid transfer protein superfamily involved in transport of lipids between different intracellular membranes. In yeast, deletion of VPS13 exhibits several distinct phenotypes due to preventing interorganelle lipid transfer between many different organelles. Vps13 shuttles lipids through a long hydrophobic channel, but how this activity is regulated in the cell is not yet understood. Studies in yeast and human cells have implicated small calcium-binding proteins, Cdc31 in yeast and calmodulin in mammalian cells, as potential regulators of Vps13 activity. This report identifies the binding site on Vps13 for Cdc31, the yeast ortholog of centrin. The yeast calmodulin protein Cmd1 binds Vps13 through the same site and separate Cmd1-Vps13 and Cdc31-Vps13 complexes co-exist in vivo. Association of Cmd1 with Vps13, but not Cdc31, is sensitive to the presence of Ca2+.  A mutant of VPS13 that is unable to interact with either Cdc31 or Cmd1 is specifically defective in mitochondrial homeostasis and endoplasmic-reticulum (ER)-phagy, indicating that Vps13 binding to Cdc31 and/or Cmd1 is important for a subset of VPS13 functions.
